title: Excel: Excel canvas turns workbook data into a Copilot-generated report that refreshes itself
summary: Hold: the sensitivity-label control is presented as excluding workbooks from Copilot in Excel without explaining that it is unavailable for Excel for the web and depends on supported desktop versions. The mixed licensing classification also goes beyond the published entitlement evidence, although the briefing correctly leaves the canvas-specific tier unresolved.

claims.quote: Users will be able to generate an interactive Copilot-created report from workbook data. Reports will combine key visualizations, metrics, and insights in a single view.

claims.quote: If you're using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center.

claims.claim: Setting UserContentDisabled to 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the analyse-content policy.
claims.quote: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled 2=Disabled; [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.claim: Disabling connected experiences that analyse content makes Copilot features unavailable in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word, including Excel canvas on Windows.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel OneNote Outlook PowerPoint Word

claims.claim: Connected experiences that analyse content are available if their policy is not configured.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy setting, these connected experiences will be available to your users.

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policy can be deployed with Cloud Policy instead of Group Policy.
